title.narrative: Integrated management and ecological connectivity of a priority landscape in the Ecuadorian Amazon headwaters

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Project Objective: Conserve, restore and promote the adoption of sustainable land management practices across 1,038,377 hectares of tropical montane forest landscapes along the Eastern Ecuadorian Andes, while enhancing Andean-Amazon habitat connectivity
CI1: Terrestrial protected areas created or under improved management (Target: 577,289 ha) CI3: Area of land and ecosystems under restoration (Target: 400 ha) CI4: Area of landscapes under improved practices (Target: 461,088 ha) CI6: Greenhouse gas emission mitigated (Target: -5,068,290 million tons CO2e) CI11: People benefiting from GEF-financed investments (Target: 56,177; 27,154 men and 29,023 women)

Socio-economic Benefits 1. The project aims to improve human well-being by addressing deforestation and forest degradation through effective conservation, strengthened governance, and SLM practices. By improving the management of 583,000 ha of globally significant biodiversity in selected protected areas, the project will help maintain essential ecosystem services such as water provision, soil fertility, and climate regulation, thereby enhancing the quality of life for local populations. Innovative financial mechanisms will secure long-term financial flows for conservation efforts, enhancing the capacity of local conservation areas for effective management. 2. Strengthening governance by fostering dialogue among key stakeholders, including women and youth, and integrating land use planning into policies and development programs will result in more effective and inclusive governance structures, equitable resource management, and increased community engagement, empowering local populations and promoting social cohesion. Continuous education and training will empower local governments, farmers and communities to participate actively in territorial governance. 3. Implementing SLM practices at the farm scale will enhance agricultural productivity, improve food security, and strengthen local economies by promoting the trade of sustainable products, regularizing land tenure, and increasing access to rural financial services. Associative production with increased market access to added-value products will create new economic opportunities, diversify household income, and improve living standards for local communities. 4. We confirm that the project design has considered socio-economic benefits to be delivered by the project and these have been clearly described in the Project Description and will be monitored and reported on during project implementation (at PIR, MTR and TE).
